name: Estimation
instructions: These are estimation problems. Nobody expects the exact value, but the closer the better. Your answer must be a single number written in digits, with no units and no range.

questions.prompt: Estimate the sum of the first 1,000 prime numbers.
A multiplication table shows every product a x b for a and b from 1 to 100. Many products appear more than once. Estimate how many DIFFERENT numbers appear in the table.
Estimate how many digits the number 1000! (1000 factorial) has when written out in full.
Estimate how many different ways there are to make exactly $5.00 using any mix of pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters (the order of the coins does not matter).
Estimate how many whole numbers from 1 to 1,000,000 have digits that add up to exactly 27.
Estimate how many whole numbers from 1 to 10,000 are the product of exactly two primes (the two primes may be the same, so 4 = 2 x 2 and 15 = 3 x 5 both count).
Estimate how many prime numbers lie between 1,000,000 and 1,100,000.
Estimate the sum of the digits of the number 3 to the power 500 when written out in full.
